nodes.name: Kripke frame
nodes.statement: A \emph{Kripke frame} or \emph{modal frame} is a pair $F = \langle W, R \rangle$ where $W$ is a nonempty set of worlds and $R$ is a \textbf{binary relation} on $W$. Elements of $W$ are called \emph{nodes} or \emph{worlds}, and $R$ is known as the \textbf{accessibility relation}. When $Rww'$ holds, we say that $w'$ is \emph{accessible} from $w$.
differentia: $W$ is a nonempty set of worlds
nodes.statement_short: A Kripke frame is a nonempty set of worlds with a binary accessibility relation.
nodes.label: def:kripke-frame

nodes.name: Kripke model
nodes.statement: A \emph{Kripke model} for the basic modal language is a triple $M = \langle W, R, V \rangle$, where: \begin{enumerate} \item $W$ is a nonempty set of \emph{worlds}, \item $R$ is a binary \emph{accessibility relation} on $W$, and \item $V$ is a function assigning to each propositional variable $p$ a set $V(p)$ of possible worlds. \end{enumerate} When $w \in V(p)$, we say that $p$ is \emph{true} at $w$. A \emph{model} $M$ is based on a frame $F = \langle W, R \rangle$ iff $M = \langle W, R, V \rangle$ for some valuation $V$.
differentia: $V$ is a function assigning to each propositional variable $p$ a set $V(p)$ of possible worlds
nodes.statement_short: A Kripke model is a frame plus a valuation sending each variable to a set of worlds; a model is based on its frame.
nodes.label: def:kripke-model

nodes.name: Truth of a formula at a world
nodes.statement: Truth of a formula $A$ at world $w$ in a model $M$, in symbols $M, w \Vdash A$, is defined, for the modal operators $\Box$ and $\Diamond$, inductively as follows: \begin{enumerate} \item $A \equiv \Box B$: $M, w \Vdash \Box B$ iff for all $w' \in W$ such that $Rww'$, we have $M, w' \Vdash B$. \item $A \equiv \Diamond B$: $M, w \Vdash \Diamond B$ iff there exists $w' \in W$ such that $Rww'$ and $M, w' \Vdash B$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Kripke semantics of $\Box$ (all accessible worlds) and $\Diamond$ (some accessible world).
nodes.label: truth-of-formula

nodes.name: Vacuous truth of box and failure of diamond
nodes.statement: Note that by the first clause, a formula $\Box B$ is true at $w$ whenever there are no $w'$ with $Rww'$. In such a case, $\Box B$ is vacuously true at $w$. Also, $\Box B$ may be satisfied at $w$ even if $B$ is not. The truth of $B$ at $w$ does not guarantee the truth of $\Diamond B$ at $w$. This holds, however, if $Rww$ holds (e.g., if $R$ is reflexive). If there is no $w'$ such that $Rww'$, then $M, w \not\Vdash \Diamond A$, for any $A$.
nodes.statement_short: $\Box B$ is vacuously true at worlds with no successors, where every $\Diamond A$ fails; truth of $B$ gives $\Diamond B$ only if $Rww$.

nodes.name: Boolean structure on predicates
nodes.statement: For a fixed frame $F$, the collection $\mathcal{P}(W)$ of predicates $p : W \to \{\top,\bot\}$ admits the following Boolean structure: \begin{itemize} \item $\bot = \emptyset$, $\top = W$, \item $p \leq q \iff \forall w \in W,\; p(w) \Rightarrow q(w)$, \item $(p \wedge q)(w) \iff p(w) \wedge q(w)$, \item $(p \vee q)(w) \iff p(w) \vee q(w)$, \item $(\neg p)(w) \iff \neg (p(w))$. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Pointwise order, meet, join, complement, top and bottom on predicates $W \to \{\top,\bot\}$.
nodes.label: def:boolean-structure

nodes.name: Proof of the Boolean algebra structure
nodes.statement: Direct verification of the Boolean algebra laws, mirroring the corresponding Lean instances (\texttt{Bot}, \texttt{Top}, \texttt{PartialOrder}, \texttt{SemilatticeInf}, \texttt{SemilatticeSup}, and \texttt{BooleanAlgebra}).
nodes.statement_short: Direct verification of the Boolean algebra laws, mirroring the Lean instances.

nodes.name: Modal operators on predicates
nodes.statement: In this Boolean setting, modal operators can be seen as operators on the algebra of propositions: \begin{align*} (\Box p)(w) &\iff \forall w' \in W,\; Rww' \Rightarrow p(w'), \\ (\Diamond p)(w) &\iff \exists w' \in W,\; Rww' \wedge p(w'). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: $\Box p$ / $\Diamond p$ hold at $w$ iff $p$ holds at all / some $R$-successors of $w$.

nodes.name: Monotonicity of box and diamond
nodes.statement: Both $\Box$ and $\Diamond$ are monotone with respect to~$\leq$.
conclusions: Both $\Box$ and $\Diamond$ are monotone with respect to~$\leq$.

nodes.name: Set of atomic propositions
nodes.statement: We define the set of formulas over a given set of atomic propositions $\mathrm{Atom}$ inductively.

nodes.name: Modal formula
nodes.statement: The set of \emph{formulas}, denoted $\mathcal{F}(\mathrm{Atom})$, is defined as follows: \begin{enumerate} \item For each atomic proposition $a \in \mathrm{Atom}$, $\mathtt{atom}\ a \in \mathcal{F}(\mathrm{Atom})$. \item $\top$ (\texttt{true}) and $\bot$ (\texttt{bot}) are formulas representing truth and falsity. \item If $\phi, \psi \in \mathcal{F}(\mathrm{Atom})$, then $\phi \wedge \psi$ (\texttt{and}) and $\phi \to \psi$ (\texttt{imp}) are formulas. \item If $\phi \in \mathcal{F}(\mathrm{Atom})$, then $\Box \phi$ (\texttt{box}) is a formula. The possibility operator is defined as $\Diamond \phi := \neg \Box \neg \phi$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Formulas built inductively from atoms, $\top$, $\bot$, $\wedge$, $\to$ and $\Box$, with $\Diamond := \neg\Box\neg$.
nodes.label: def:form

nodes.name: True in a model
nodes.statement: A formula $A$ is \emph{true in a model} $M = \langle W, R, V \rangle$, written $M \Vdash A$, iff $M, w \Vdash A$ for every $w \in W$.
nodes.label: true-in-model

nodes.name: Unit frame and two-atom model
nodes.statement: A minimal example is provided: \begin{itemize} \item Unit frame: $W = \{\star\}$, $R(\star,\star) = \text{True}$. \item Atomic propositions: $\mathrm{Atom} = \{\texttt{p}, \texttt{q}\}$. \item Unit model: $V(\texttt{p},\star) = \text{True}$, $V(\texttt{q},\star) = \text{False}$. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: One-world reflexive frame with atoms p (true) and q (false).

nodes.name: Satisfaction relation of the formalized semantics
nodes.statement: \begin{itemize} \item $\text{true}$ is always valid. \item Atoms follow the valuation: $M \Vdash a\, w$ iff $V(a, w)$. \item Boolean connectives are interpreted pointwise. \item $\Box \phi$ holds at $w$ if $\phi$ holds at all $w'$ accessible from $w$. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Inductive satisfaction: true always holds, atoms follow the valuation, connectives pointwise, box over accessible worlds.
nodes.label: def:example

nodes.name: Semantic soundness
nodes.statement: If a formula $\phi$ has a proof in the deductive system from hypotheses $\Gamma$, then it is valid in any model $M$ at any world $w$: \[ \Gamma \vdash \phi \implies \forall M, w,\, M \Vdash \Gamma \Rightarrow M \Vdash \phi \text{ at } w. \]
assumptions: a formula $\phi$ has a proof in the deductive system from hypotheses $\Gamma$
conclusions: it is valid in any model $M$ at any world $w$
nodes.statement_short: Anything derivable from $\Gamma$ holds at every world of every model satisfying $\Gamma$.
nodes.label: thm:semantic-soundness

nodes.name: Valid formula
nodes.statement: Formulas that are true in all models, i.e., true at every world in every model, are particularly interesting. They represent those modal propositions which are true regardless of how $\Box$ and $\Diamond$ are interpreted, as long as the interpretation is generated by some accessibility relation on possible worlds. We call such formulas \emph{valid}.

nodes.name: Axiom T holds in reflexive models
nodes.statement: It will turn out, e.g., that $\Box p \to p$ is true in all models where every world is accessible from itself, i.e., $R$ is reflexive.
assumptions: models where every world is accessible from itself, i.e., $R$ is reflexive

nodes.name: Valid in a class of models
nodes.statement: A formula $A$ is \emph{KripkeModel, valid in a class} $\mathcal{C}$ of models if it is true in every model in $\mathcal{C}$ (i.e., true at every world in every model in $\mathcal{C}$). If $A$ is valid in $\mathcal{C}$, we write $\mathcal{C} \vDash A$, and we write $\vDash A$ if $A$ is valid in the class of all models.
nodes.statement_short: $A$ is valid in a class of models if true at every world of every model in it; $\vDash A$ for the class of all models.
nodes.label: valid-in-class

nodes.name: Schema
nodes.statement: A \emph{schema}, i.e., a set of formulas comprising all and only the substitution instances of some modal characteristic formula $C$, is \emph{true in a model} iff all of its instances are (where a formula $A$ is an \emph{instance} of a schema if it is a member of the set); and a schema is \emph{valid} if and only if it is true in every model.
nodes.statement_short: A schema is the set of substitution instances of a formula; it is true in a model if all instances are, valid if true in every model.
nodes.label: valid-schema

nodes.name: Duality schema
nodes.statement: The following schema, called the \emph{duality schema}, is valid: \[ \Diamond A \leftrightarrow \neg \Box \neg A. \]
conclusions: The following schema, called the \emph{duality schema}, is valid: \[ \Diamond A \leftrightarrow \neg \Box \neg A. \]
nodes.label: duality-schema

nodes.name: Proof of the duality schema
nodes.statement: By straightforward unfolding of definitions and classical equivalences between \(\diamond\) and \(\Box\).
nodes.statement_short: Unfold the definitions of $\Diamond$ and $\Box$ and use classical equivalences.

nodes.name: Validity is closed under modus ponens
nodes.statement: If $A$ and $A \rightarrow B$ are true at a world in a model, then so is $B$. Hence, the valid formulas are closed under modus ponens.
assumptions: $A$ and $A \rightarrow B$ are true at a world in a model
conclusions: the valid formulas are closed under modus ponens
nodes.label: modus-ponens-validity

nodes.name: Substitution and validity
nodes.statement: A formula $A$ is valid iff all its substitution instances are. In other words, a schema is valid iff its characteristic formula is.
conclusions: A formula $A$ is valid iff all its substitution instances are.
a schema is valid iff its characteristic formula is
nodes.label: substitution-validity

nodes.name: Semantic entailment
nodes.statement: If $\Gamma$ is a set of formulas and $A$ a formula, then $\Gamma \vDash A$ iif for every model $M = \langle W, R, V \rangle$ and world $w \in W$, if $M, w \vDash B$ for every $B \in \Gamma$, then $M, w \vDash A$. If $\Gamma$ contains a single formula $B$, then we write $B \vDash A$.
also_stated_at: A formula $B$ \emph{entails} $A$ if and only if, whenever $B$ is true, $A$ is true as well.
nodes.statement_short: $\Gamma$ entails $A$ if every world of every model satisfying all of $\Gamma$ satisfies $A$.
nodes.label: semantic-entailment

nodes.name: Frame properties guarantee modal axioms
nodes.statement: \ Let $M = \langle W, R, V \rangle$ be a model. If $R$ has the property on the left side of Table~\ref{tab:table-schemata-relations}, then every instance of the formula on the right side is true in $M$.
assumptions: Let $M = \langle W, R, V \rangle$ be a model.
$R$ has the property on the left side of Table~\ref{tab:table-schemata-relations}
conclusions: every instance of the formula on the right side is true in $M$
nodes.statement_short: If the accessibility relation is reflexive/dense/transitive/serial/symmetric/euclidean, the matching axiom holds in the model.
nodes.label: thm:truth-guarantee

nodes.name: Proof of the truth guarantees
nodes.statement: We prove the validity of the modal axioms as follows: \begin{itemize} \item \textbf{modal axiom K valid}: \\ By unfolding the definition of \(\Box\) and applying function application at accessible worlds. \item \textbf{modal axiom T valid}: \\ By reflexivity of the accessibility relation and unfolding of \(\Box\). \item \textbf{modal dense valid}: \\ By using density of the accessibility relation and applying the nested \(\Box\) accordingly. \item \textbf{modal axiom 4 valid}: \\ By transitivity of the accessibility relation and unfolding the definition of nested \(\Box.\) \item \textbf{modal axiom D valid}: \\ By seriality, we find an accessible world witnessing the \(\Diamond\) modality. \item \textbf{modal axiom B valid}: \\ By symmetry of the accessibility relation and constructing a witness for \(\Diamond\). \item \textbf{modal axiom 5 valid}: \\ By Euclidean property of the relation and unfolding \(\Diamond\) and \(\Box\). \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Case by case over the axioms: unfold $\Box$/$\Diamond$ and use the corresponding property of $R$.

nodes.name: Valid in a frame
nodes.statement: If $F$ is a frame, we say that a formula $A$ is \emph{valid in $F$}, written $F \Vdash A$, iff $M \Vdash A$ for every model $M$ based on $F$. If $\mathcal{F}$ is a class of frames, we say $A$ is \emph{valid in} $\mathcal{F}$, written $\mathcal{F} \Vdash A$, iff $F \Vdash A$ for every frame $F \in \mathcal{F}$.
also_stated_at: We can define $F \vDash A$, the notion of a formula being \emph{valid in a frame}, as: $M \vDash A$ for all models $M$ based on $F$.
nodes.statement_short: $A$ is valid in a frame if true in every model based on it, and in a class of frames if valid in each.
nodes.label: valid-in-frame

nodes.name: Axiom T defines reflexive frames
nodes.statement: For example: $F \vDash \Box p \rightarrow p \quad \text{if and only if} \quad F \text{ is reflexive.}$
conclusions: $F \vDash \Box p \rightarrow p \quad \text{if and only if} \quad F \text{ is reflexive.}$

nodes.name: Converse holds for frames
nodes.statement: Even though the converse implications of Theorem~\ref{thm:truth-guarantee} fail, they hold if we replace ``model'' by ``frame'': for the properties considered in Theorem~\ref{thm:truth-guarantee}, it is true that if a formula is valid in a frame then the accessibility relation of that frame has the corresponding property. So, the formulas considered \emph{define} the classes of frames that have the corresponding property.
nodes.statement_short: The converses of Theorem 2 fail for models but hold for frames, so the axioms define their frame classes.

nodes.name: Formula defining a class of frames
nodes.statement: If $\mathcal{F}$ is a class of frames, we say that a formula $A$ \emph{defines} $\mathcal{F}$ iff $F \vDash A$ for all and only frames $F \in \mathcal{F}$.
nodes.statement_short: $A$ defines a class of frames if it is valid in exactly the frames of that class.
nodes.label: def:class-of-frame

nodes.name: Frame definability
nodes.statement: If the formula on the right side of Table~\ref{tab:table-schemata-relations} is valid in a frame $F$, then $F$ has the property on the left side.
assumptions: the formula on the right side of Table~\ref{tab:table-schemata-relations} is valid in a frame $F$
conclusions: $F$ has the property on the left side
nodes.statement_short: Validity of each listed axiom in a frame forces the corresponding property of its accessibility relation.
nodes.label: thm:definability

nodes.name: Proof of frame definability
nodes.statement: We prove the implications of validity on frame properties as follows: \begin{itemize} \item \textbf{valid T implies reflexive}: \\ By defining a valuation reflecting the accessibility relation and applying the \textbf{T} axiom. \item \textbf{valid 4 implies transitive}: \\ By contraposition: assume failure of transitivity and build a valuation violating the \textbf{4} axiom. \item \textbf{valid D implies serial}: \\ By contraposition: assume no successor exists and construct a counterexample model violating \(\Diamond\)A. \item \textbf{valid B implies symmetric}: \\ By contraposition: assume asymmetry and derive a contradiction from the validity of \(\Box\Diamond A\). \item \textbf{valid 5 implies euclidean}: \\ By contraposition: assume failure of Euclidean property and construct a counterexample valuation to contradict \(\Box \Diamond A\). \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Case by case: for T define a valuation from $R$; for 4, D, B, 5 contrapose and build a valuation violating the axiom.

nodes.name: D defines serial models
nodes.statement: We notice, that in the proof for \textbf{D} no mention was made of the valuation V. Hence, it proves p that if \( M \Vdash \textbf{D} \) then \( M \) is serial. So \textbf{D} defines the class of serial models, not just frames.
nodes.statement_short: The D case never used the valuation, so D defines the class of serial models, not just frames.

nodes.name: Table of modal axioms and frame conditions
nodes.statement: \begin{table}[h] \centering \[ \begin{array}{|c|c|c|} \hline \textbf{Name} & \textbf{Axiom} & \textbf{Frame Condition} \\ \hline \textbf{K} & \Box (A \to B) \to (\Box A \to \Box B) & \text{Holds true for any frames} \\ \hline \textbf{T} & \Box A \to A & \text{Reflexive: } w\,R\,w \\ \hline - & \Box\Box A \to \Box A & \text{Dense: } w\,R\,u \Rightarrow \exists v\,(w\,R\,v \land v\,R\,u) \\ \hline \textbf{4} & \Box A \to \Box\Box A & \text{Transitive: } w\,R\,v \wedge v\,R\,u \Rightarrow w\,R\,u \\ \hline \textbf{D} & \Box A \to \Diamond A \text{ or } \Diamond\top \text{ or } \neg\Box\bot & \text{Serial: } \forall w\,\exists v\,(w\,R\,v) \\ \hline \textbf{B} & A \to \Box\Diamond A \text{ or } \Diamond\Box A \to A & \text{Symmetric: } w\,R\,v \Rightarrow v\,R\,w \\ \hline \textbf{5} & \Diamond A \to \Box\Diamond A & \text{Euclidean: } w\,R\,u \land w\,R\,v \Rightarrow u\,R\,v \\ \hline \end{array} \] \caption{The following table lists common modal axioms together with their corresponding classes. The implication of axiom to frame condition follows from Theorem~\ref{thm:truth-guarantee} and the converse from Theorem~\ref{thm:definability}} \end{table}
nodes.statement_short: Modal axioms K, T, density, 4, D, B, 5 paired with their frame conditions.

nodes.statement: \textbf{modal axiom K valid}: \\ By unfolding the definition of \(\Box\) and applying function application at accessible worlds.
nodes.statement_short: Axiom K: unfold box, apply at accessible worlds

nodes.name: Axiom T from reflexivity
nodes.statement: \textbf{modal axiom T valid}: \\ By reflexivity of the accessibility relation and unfolding of \(\Box\).
nodes.statement_short: Axiom T from reflexivity

nodes.name: Density axiom from density of R
nodes.statement: \textbf{modal dense valid}: \\ By using density of the accessibility relation and applying the nested \(\Box\) accordingly.
nodes.statement_short: Density axiom from density of R

nodes.name: Axiom 4 from transitivity
nodes.statement: \textbf{modal axiom 4 valid}: \\ By transitivity of the accessibility relation and unfolding the definition of nested \(\Box.\)
nodes.statement_short: Axiom 4 from transitivity

nodes.name: Axiom D from seriality via a witness world
nodes.statement: \textbf{modal axiom D valid}: \\ By seriality, we find an accessible world witnessing the \(\Diamond\) modality.
nodes.statement_short: Axiom D from seriality via a witness world

nodes.name: Axiom B from symmetry
nodes.statement: \textbf{modal axiom B valid}: \\ By symmetry of the accessibility relation and constructing a witness for \(\Diamond\).
nodes.statement_short: Axiom B from symmetry

nodes.name: Axiom 5 from the Euclidean property
nodes.statement: \textbf{modal axiom 5 valid}: \\ By Euclidean property of the relation and unfolding \(\Diamond\) and \(\Box\).
nodes.statement_short: Axiom 5 from the Euclidean property

nodes.name: Announce case-by-case frame correspondences
nodes.statement: We prove the implications of validity on frame properties as follows:
nodes.statement_short: Announce case-by-case frame correspondences

nodes.name: Valid T gives reflexivity via a valuation mirroring R
nodes.statement: \textbf{valid T implies reflexive}: \\ By defining a valuation reflecting the accessibility relation and applying the \textbf{T} axiom.
nodes.statement_short: Valid T gives reflexivity via a valuation mirroring R

nodes.name: Valid 4 gives transitivity by contraposition
nodes.statement: \textbf{valid 4 implies transitive}: \\ By contraposition: assume failure of transitivity and build a valuation violating the \textbf{4} axiom.
nodes.statement_short: Valid 4 gives transitivity by contraposition

nodes.name: Valid D gives seriality by contraposition
nodes.statement: \textbf{valid D implies serial}: \\ By contraposition: assume no successor exists and construct a counterexample model violating \(\Diamond\)A.
nodes.statement_short: Valid D gives seriality by contraposition

nodes.statement: \textbf{valid B implies symmetric}: \\ By contraposition: assume asymmetry and derive a contradiction from the validity of \(\Box\Diamond A\).
nodes.statement_short: Valid B gives symmetry by contraposition

nodes.name: Valid 5 gives the Euclidean property by contraposition
nodes.statement: \textbf{valid 5 implies euclidean}: \\ By contraposition: assume failure of Euclidean property and construct a counterexample valuation to contradict \(\Box \Diamond A\).
nodes.statement_short: Valid 5 gives the Euclidean property by contraposition
